chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Sulayman ibn Haf al-Marwazi said:
The Faqih (peace be upon him) said: 'The sick person only prays sitting when he reaches a state in which he is unable to walk the distance equivalent to his prayer until he finishes standing.'
ai.seo_question: When is a sick person required to pray sitting down instead of standing?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the threshold for *rukūʿ* (standing) in prayer for the ill, specifying that sitting is obligatory only when the patient loses the capacity to walk the distance equivalent to the duration of the prayer. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *al-ḥājah ilā al-ḥarakah* (need for movement), ensuring that the obligation to stand is lifted only when physical exertion becomes genuinely burdensome. It highlights the balance between maintaining the form of worship and accommodating the patient's actual physical limitations.
